$comment: P42 lane AI — one runtime witness for four conformance divergences closed in the same change, on BOTH the baseline (debug) and the `release` (shippedPipeline) arm. Each arm contributes a DISTINCT power of two so the exit code names which one broke: +1 bare `_Complex` with no float specifier (D-CSUBSET-BARE-COMPLEX-SPECIFIER-REFUSED — both references give it a DOUBLE element, and the arm reads a value only a double element holds exactly, so a float-element row would fail it); +2 unary `+` on a complex (D-CSUBSET-COMPLEX-UNARY-PLUS-REFUSED — BOTH components are checked, because a real-part-only implementation would satisfy a real-part-only assertion); +4 `(long long)fn` on a function DESIGNATOR round-tripped back through a function pointer and CALLED (D-CSUBSET-FUNCTION-DESIGNATOR-TO-INTEGER-CAST-REFUSED — the CALL is the load-bearing half; a plausible-but-wrong integer passes a `!= 0` test and faults here); +8 the POSITIVE control for the switch-discriminant guard (D-CSUBSET-SWITCH-ON-A-NON-INTEGER-DISCRIMINANT-ACCEPTED — the refusal half is unit-pinned, since a corpus example cannot hold source the compiler must reject, so this arm is what proves the guard did not redden every switch in the corpus). ⚠ Arm 3 uses `long long` and NOT `long` deliberately: `long` is 32 bits on LLP64 (pe64) and 64 on LP64, so a `long` round trip TRUNCATES a code address on Windows — an earlier draft used `long` and produced an ACCESS VIOLATION that looked exactly like a miscompile and was really the probe comparing two data models. ANTI-FOLD: every complex and every integer input is a MUTABLE GLOBAL written at runtime, so the release arm exercises real code rather than a constant fold. exit = 1+2+4+8 = 15 iff every arm passes.
